column1: # AQL Language Specification: the aql:vm module
# Loadable capability module. Import binds the `Vm` namespace, then code
# is run in an isolated sub-engine under an explicit policy via dot-access:
# `import "aql:vm"  Vm.run-compute "1 add 2"`. Each word parses the
# supplied source string, runs it through a fresh engine governed by the
# resolved policy (composed with the parent's so a child can never widen
# the parent's permissions), and returns the last residual stack value.

column3: runs code in a sandboxed sub-engine, returns the result

column1: # §3  run-with — explicit policy supplied as a data map
import "aql:vm" { scopes: { engine: { words: { default: "allow" } } } } "10 sub 3" Vm.run-with
column3: policy map + code; an allow-all engine scope runs the arithmetic

column1: # §4  parse — AQL source → inspectable structure (no evaluation).
#     Returns a QUOTED list of the engine's parse values; element

column3: parses source to a quoted token list without running it

column1: # §5  check — static type-check WITHOUT running. Returns a result map
#     { ok errors warnings diagnostics }; findings are DATA, never raised
#     (even a syntax error rides back as one error-severity diagnostic),
#     so callers get one uniform shape. Runs under the parent's policy.

column3: an undefined word fails the check
each diagnostic carries a stable code
a syntax error is a check finding, not a raised error

column1: # §6  compile — run the bytecode compile pass WITHOUT executing. Returns
#     { ok reason sites }: ok = lowers to bytecode, reason = first offender
#     when it does not, sites = the dispatch-site census. Refusal is data,

column3: the dispatch-site census reports one mono call
